faq.q: What do I do when the product photo still shows the room?
faq.a: Upload it and download a file where the product sits on white. Every edge stays inside the frame and the room is gone.

faq.q: How do I put a product photo onto pure white?
faq.a: Upload your photo, choose pure white (RGB 255, 255, 255) to meet a marketplace's white-background rule for main images, then download. The product shape stays the one in your photo.

faq.q: Does a marketplace main image have to sit on white?
faq.a: Often it does, and a grey-looking field is a common reason a listing image gets sent back. Open the current rule for your category before you publish. You get a plain white field. The tool does not submit the listing for you.

faq.q: Can the product look flat on white?
faq.a: It can, if the source photo is flatly lit and the base has no weight. A soft shadow under the product helps it read as sitting on the page.

faq.q: Does a white product photo cost anything?
faq.a: Yes. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. One photo spends 24 credits. Those credits also pay for videos.

faq.q: Can one white field cover a whole folder of photos?
faq.a: Yes. Send the folder through the API, or run the files together in the app. Each photo still shows its credit cost first.

faq.q: How many credits does one photo use?
faq.a: One product photo uses 24 credits. You see that number before the job starts. If the photo fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: What should the starting photo show?
faq.a: The whole product, with edges that are not cut off. A simple setting in the original photo makes the white result easier to check.

faq.q: Can I post the file on Amazon, Shopify, or Etsy?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no watermark, so you can put it on Amazon, Shopify, or Etsy, and in your ads.

faq.q: Which tool fits a pure white product photo?
faq.a: Use this one when you want the room gone and the item kept. You upload one clear photo of the whole product.
